questions.questionText: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of a confined space as described by OSHA 1910.146?

options.text: It is always located underground
It is large enough to enter and perform work but has limited or restricted means of entry or exit
It is always labeled with a warning sign
It is always safe once ventilated

questions.questionText: A permit-required confined space may contain which type of hazard?

options.text: Hazardous atmosphere
Engulfment hazard
Internal configuration hazard
Any of the above

questions.questionText: What must happen before a permit-required confined space entry can begin?

options.text: The attendant must enter the space first to check conditions
The entry permit must be completed and authorized
The entrant must test the air by smell
The rescue team must be positioned inside the space

questions.questionText: What is the correct sequence for atmospheric testing before confined space entry?

options.text: Toxic contaminants, then oxygen, then flammables
Flammables, then oxygen, then toxic contaminants
Oxygen, then flammables, then toxic contaminants
Oxygen, then toxic contaminants, then flammables

questions.questionText: An oxygen level above 23.5 percent inside a confined space increases fire and explosion hazards.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Who is responsible for authorizing entry by signing the entry permit?

options.text: The authorized entrant
The entry supervisor
A contractor helper
The emergency dispatcher

questions.questionText: What is one primary responsibility of the confined space attendant?

options.text: Perform unrelated maintenance tasks while entrants work
Stay outside the space and monitor entrants and conditions
Enter immediately for rescue in every emergency
Cancel the written confined space program when entry is complete

questions.questionText: An authorized entrant begins to feel dizzy while working inside a confined space. What should happen?

options.text: The entrant should continue working unless the job is almost complete
The entrant should report the symptom to the attendant and exit the space
The attendant should ignore it unless the atmospheric monitor alarms
The supervisor should extend the permit to allow more time

questions.questionText: Pure oxygen may be used to ventilate a confined space that has a low oxygen reading.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: If a prohibited condition develops during a permit-required confined space entry, what should occur?

options.text: Continue working until the task is complete
Evacuate entrants and cancel or suspend the permit as required
Send an untrained worker in to investigate the condition
Remove the attendant and continue without monitoring

questions.questionText: Why are completed confined space entry permits retained and reviewed after entry?

options.text: To improve the confined space program and identify needed corrections
To avoid the need to train employees in the future
To replace atmospheric testing on future entries
To allow entry without permits for similar future spaces

questions.questionText: A contractor is hired to perform work inside a permit-required confined space at your facility. What must occur before work begins?

options.text: The contractor enters under its own rules without facility input
The host employer and contractor coordinate information about hazards and entry procedures
The permit requirement is waived because a contractor is performing the work
An attendant is not required when contractors are present

questions.questionText: The attendant should immediately enter the confined space to attempt a rescue whenever an entrant appears to be in distress.

options.text: True
False

questions.questionText: Non-entry rescue methods are preferred for confined space rescue whenever feasible because:

options.text: They are required by all state and local fire codes
They allow entrant removal without exposing additional workers to space hazards
They require no advance planning or equipment
They are less expensive than hiring a rescue team

questions.questionText: An authorized entrant must exit a confined space immediately when ordered to evacuate, even if the assigned work is not yet complete.

options.text: True
False

confined-space-definition.title: Confined Spaces: Definition and Recognition
confined-space-definition.content: A confined space is large enough for an employee to enter and perform work, has limited or restricted means of entry or exit, and is not designed for continuous occupancy. Examples include tanks, vessels, silos, bins, boilers, vaults, pits, manholes, tunnels, and pipelines. A confined space is NOT automatically safe — it may contain hazardous atmospheres, engulfment hazards, or mechanical hazards. Employers must evaluate the workplace to identify confined spaces and inform employees of their existence.

permit-required-spaces.title: Permit-Required Confined Spaces
permit-required-spaces.content: A permit-required confined space contains, or has the potential to contain, a serious hazard. These hazards may include: a hazardous or potentially hazardous atmosphere, material that can engulf an entrant, an internal configuration that could trap or asphyxiate a worker, or other serious safety or health risks. Employers must prevent unauthorized entry, post required warning signs, and implement a written permit space program when employees enter permit spaces. Contractors working in permit spaces must coordinate with the host employer on known hazards and procedures.

atmospheric-testing.title: Atmospheric Hazards and Testing Sequence
atmospheric-testing.content: Before entry, the atmosphere must be tested in the correct order: first oxygen content, then flammable gases or vapors, then toxic contaminants. Oxygen below 19.5% is oxygen-deficient; above 23.5% is oxygen-enriched and significantly increases fire and explosion risk. Flammable gases at hazardous concentrations can ignite with a single spark. Toxic gases like carbon monoxide or hydrogen sulfide can cause unconsciousness or death. Never trust your senses alone — some hazardous atmospheres cannot be seen, smelled, or felt.

hazard-control-ventilation.title: Hazard Control and Ventilation
hazard-control-ventilation.content: When atmospheric hazards are found, they must be controlled before entry. Forced-air ventilation is a common method, but pure oxygen must NEVER be used for ventilation — it creates an oxygen-enriched atmosphere that dramatically increases fire and explosion risk. If ventilation alone cannot control the hazard, respiratory protection may be required. Other controls include lockout/tagout for hazardous energy, hot work permits, and barriers around entry points. Stop work if ventilation fails or atmospheric conditions deteriorate.

roles-and-responsibilities.title: Entry Supervisor, Entrant, and Attendant Roles
roles-and-responsibilities.content: The entry supervisor verifies acceptable conditions, authorizes and signs the entry permit, and terminates the entry when work is complete or conditions become unsafe. The authorized entrant performs the assigned work, uses required PPE, maintains communication with the attendant, and must exit immediately when ordered or when symptoms of exposure appear. The attendant remains OUTSIDE the permit space, tracks entrants, monitors conditions, maintains communication, orders evacuation when needed, and summons rescue services — the attendant does NOT enter for rescue unless specifically authorized, trained, and equipped.

entry-permits.title: Entry Permits and Documentation
entry-permits.content: The entry permit is the written authorization for confined space entry. It documents the space, purpose of entry, date, authorized duration, identified hazards, controls implemented, names of entrants and attendant, atmospheric test results, required equipment, and rescue arrangements. A permit must be completed and signed by the entry supervisor before entry begins. If conditions change or a prohibited condition develops, the permit must be cancelled and entrants must evacuate. Cancelled permits must be retained for at least one year to support program review.

rescue-emergency-planning.title: Rescue Planning and Emergency Procedures
rescue-emergency-planning.content: Rescue must be planned before entry begins. Non-entry rescue using harnesses, lifelines, tripods, and winches is preferred whenever feasible — it removes the entrant without exposing additional workers to space hazards. When outside rescue teams are used, they must be informed of the space hazards in advance and have access for planning and practice. If evacuation occurs, the space must be re-evaluated and a new permit completed before re-entry. Do not attempt unauthorized rescue — doing so can turn one emergency into multiple casualties.

1.questionText: OSHA 1910.146 defines a confined space as an area that is large enough to bodily enter, has limited or restricted entry and exit, and is not designed for continuous occupancy.

options.text: True
False

2.questionText: Which of the following can make a confined space a permit-required confined space?

options.text: Atmospheric hazards such as oxygen deficiency or flammable vapors
The potential for engulfment
Internal shapes that could trap a worker
All of the above

3.questionText: Entry into a permit-required confined space may begin as soon as the workers are ready, without a formal permit.

options.text: True
False

4.questionText: Before entering a permit-required confined space, the atmospheric testing sequence must follow this order:

options.text: Toxics first, then oxygen, then flammables
Oxygen first, then flammables, then toxics
Flammables first, then toxics, then oxygen
Any order is acceptable as long as all three tests are done

5.questionText: An oxygen-enriched atmosphere (above 23.5 percent oxygen) in a confined space is dangerous because it significantly increases the risk of fire or explosion.

options.text: True
False

6.questionText: The person who must verify conditions, authorize entry, and sign the confined space entry permit before work begins is:

options.text: The attendant
The entry supervisor
Any available employee
The facility safety director only

7.questionText: The confined space attendant's primary role is to remain outside the space, monitor entrants and conditions, and summon help when needed.

options.text: True
False

8.questionText: While working inside a confined space, an entrant notices they feel confused and lightheaded. Even without a monitor alarm, the correct response is to:

options.text: Finish the task quickly and then exit
Immediately report the symptom to the attendant and exit the space
Drink water and wait to see if the feeling passes
Ask the attendant to bring a fan to the entry point

9.questionText: To correct a low-oxygen reading inside a confined space, using pure oxygen as the ventilation supply is acceptable.

options.text: True
False

10.questionText: A prohibited condition — such as an unexpected vapor buildup — is detected while entrants are working in a confined space. What must happen?

options.text: Continue work until the current task is finished
Evacuate entrants and cancel or suspend the entry permit
Have one person remain inside to monitor the condition
Reduce ventilation to minimize gas movement

11.questionText: Employers must retain cancelled confined space entry permits for at least one year so they can review the program and make improvements.

options.text: True
False

12.questionText: Before a contractor begins work in a facility's permit-required confined space, the host employer must:

options.text: Step aside and let the contractor manage all aspects of the entry
Share information about space hazards and required precautions, and coordinate procedures with the contractor
Waive permit requirements since the contractor provides its own safety procedures
Remove all confined space warning signs to avoid confusion

13.questionText: A confined space attendant who observes an entrant in apparent distress should immediately enter the space to provide assistance.

options.text: True
False

14.questionText: The primary reason non-entry rescue (using harnesses, lifelines, and retrieval equipment) is preferred when feasible is that:

options.text: It is the cheapest option for all rescue scenarios
It allows entrant removal without placing additional workers at risk inside the space
Entry rescue is prohibited under all circumstances
It requires no planning or specialized equipment

15.questionText: When an attendant or entry supervisor orders evacuation from a confined space, the authorized entrant must exit immediately regardless of whether the task is complete.

options.text: True
False
